subject: Live chat streaming — intermittent high latency (BrightBridge)
messages:
From: Nick Chen <nick@brightbridge.health>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; support@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:03-07:00
Subject: Live chat stream: long token gaps

Hi team,

We're seeing repeated long pauses in the live chat stream from Redwood between tokens — roughly 4–6s gaps — starting around 08:45 PDT this morning. It affects our customer-facing support chat (session ids attached in the logs). The web client shows the socket as open; tokens arrive in bursts rather than continuous. This started after we pushed a minor UI change but rolling that back made no difference.

Attached is a short capture and a server-side trace from our side. Can you confirm whether this aligns with anything on your end? It's affecting peak hours so a quick mitigation would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Nick Chen
Sr. SRE, BrightBridge Health

Attachments: bbh-chat-trace-2028-03-11.txt
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Nick Chen <nick@brightbridge.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, se an_gallagher@redwood.ai, eng@brightbridge.health
Date: 2028-03-11T09:38:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat stream: long token gaps

Nick — thanks for the signal and the trace. We're triaging now.

Quick notes from our side:
- We see elevated tail latency on the US-east streaming pool that aligns with your timestamps.
- Initial hypothesis is intermittent backpressure in the batching layer causing token emission to stall and then flush in bursts.

Immediate actions:
1) I'm escalating to the runtime on-call and adding Marissa (product) and Sean (ops).
2) Can you share a single session id for a reproduced case (you included a few — pick one) and the exact SDK version your clients are on? That will help correlate traces.
3) As a short-term mitigation, please switch the client to our non-streaming endpoint (synchronous completion) for critical sessions — that avoids token pacing currently. We'll follow up with a live update within 90 minutes.

We'll keep this thread as the primary channel.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai; se an_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-11T10:05:22-07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat stream: long token gaps

Adding notes from the runtime team after a quick triage:
- We observed an autoscaler decision path that briefly consolidated several low-throughput shards which increased average serialization window and amplified batching latency for low-concurrency interactive sessions.
- There was a metric regression in prefix-KV cache hit telemetry around 08:40 PDT that coincides with increased per-request kernel warmups.

Short-term runbook we're applying now:
- Revert the recent autoscaler consolidation rule for the US-east streaming pool (already rolled back at 09:50 PDT).
- Force smaller batch size ceiling for interactive models for the next 2 hours.
- Enable an orthogonal token pacing failover: if stream latency > 1s for >3 tokens, automatically switch that session to direct completion and emit a client event so you can surface status to end users.

I'll prepare a customer-facing advisory with clear mitigations for BrightBridge and invite them to a 30-minute bridge.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Nick Chen <nick@brightbridge.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, se an_gallagher@redwood.ai, eng@brightbridge.health
Date: 2028-03-11T10:17:45-07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat stream: long token gaps

Nick — update and immediate customer guidance below.

On behalf of the runtime team: we've identified a transient autoscaler consolidation in the US-east streaming pool that increased batching windows for low-concurrency interactive sessions, and a concurrent drop in prefix cache hit rate that magnified kernel warmups. The combined effect produced the token bursts you observed.

What we did (short-term):
- Rolled back the consolidation rule at 09:50 PDT.
- Reduced the max batching ceiling for interactive models.
- Deployed a session-level failover that moves affected sessions to our non-streaming completion endpoint when token emission latency exceeds 1s for more than 3 consecutive tokens.

What you can do right now (customer mitigations):
1) If you need immediate consistent behavior, switch critical sessions to the synchronous completion endpoint: POST /v1/completions with model=<your-model> (this returns the full output in one response). This avoids token pacing variability.
2) On the streaming client, enable the client-side fallback that closes the stream and retries the request with a completion after 3 consecutive token gaps >1s. We can send a sample snippet for your SDK version.
3) If you prefer we route your production traffic to a dedicated US-east shard (short-term reserved pool) while we complete root-cause fixes, I can open a capacity action; it's billable but provides isolation during peak windows.

We will keep monitoring and share a short post-incident summary by end of day PDT. Would you be available for a 30-minute troubleshooting bridge at 10:45 PDT?

Thanks for the quick reports — the trace you attached was very helpful.

— Ben
From: Nick Chen <nick@brightbridge.health>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightBridge Engineering <eng@brightbridge.health>
Date: 2028-03-11T10:29:30-07:00
Subject: Re: Live chat stream: long token gaps

Ben/Marissa/Sean — thanks for the rapid response and for the mitigation steps. We toggled a small percentage of sessions to synchronous completion and saw immediate smoothing of UX. We're happy to join the 10:45 bridge. I'll attach a single session id and a minimal repro bundle to help debug (client-repro-frames.zip).

Appreciate the offer for a dedicated shard; we'll discuss internally and circle back.

— Nick
